events.title: No, there's no proof sunscreen increases cancer risk

events.title: France wildfires: Risk remains 'extremely high' despite slight weather improvement
events.summary: France's wildfire risk remains "extremely high" despite a slight improvement in weather conditions, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Thursday (July 30), citing persistent drought and fast-spreading blazes across the country. Nunez said higher humidity and weaker winds had helped conditions, but authorities still dealt with 26 fires nationwide on Wednesday (July 29) alone, warning that vegetation remained highly combustible.

events.title: AI before AI: The forgotten Soviet programme (1/2)
events.summary: Beginning in the 1950s, the Soviet Union launched an ambitious programme aimed at developing artificial intelligence. While the history of AI today seems to be shaped by the giants of Silicon Valley, ideas originating from behind the Iron Curtain had a significant influence, although they remain largely overlooked.

events.title: Warsaw blames Moscow after a missile crashes in Poland
events.summary: Polish authorities are investigating an object that came down in eastern Poland overnight and is thought to be a Russian missile, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Thursday. The discovery followed reports of an explosion, with investigators finding a crater and debris scattered across a nearby field.

events.title: French interior minister says wildfire situation still 'quite complicated'
events.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the "situation is still quite complicated" as wildfires continued to burn after a crisis meeting Thursday in Paris. Regarding the giant wildfires that have spread in Gironde region, Nunez said the blaze stabilised but not contained. Carys Garland reports.

events.title: As France battles unprecedented wildfires, Caroit urges collective global action on climate change
events.summary: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome French Deputy Foreign Affairs Minister Éléonore Caroit. She frames France's response to unprecedented heatwaves and wildfires through three lenses: crisis management, international solidarity, and climate governance. Caroit distinguishes between the immediate demands of emergency response and the longer term structural challenges posed by climate change, including adaptation, infrastructure resilience, and urban planning. While arguing that governments must continually strengthen preparedness and invest in prevention and adaptation, she maintains that domestic policy must be matched by sustained international climate cooperation, making collective global engagement an essential component of both disaster response and long term climate resilience.

events.title: Hundreds of migrants enter Spain's north African territory Ceuta from Morocco

events.title: #Ukraine pounded in Russian attack, Polish airspace 'violated'

events.title: How native livestock is reducing the risk of wildfires in Spain's Galicia region
events.summary: In Spain's Galicia region, native goats, sheep, and cows are helping local communities reduce the risk of wildfires by grazing on flammable undergrowth.The initiative has gained momentum in an area hit hard by Spain's worst wildfire year in 2025, where nearly 119,00 hectares of land burned, an area spanning roughly double the size of Madrid. The animals include the Cachena, a native goat-like cow known for its ability to forage widely and traverse the region's mountainous terrain.

events.title: Greek firefighters battle deadly wildfires on Crete for a second day
events.summary: Greek firefighters were ⁠battling deadly wildfires on ​the island of Crete for a second day on Thursday, as wildfires continue to ​spread across Europe following days of devastating blazes in Spain and France. On Wednesday, three Greek firefighters died battling blazes during high winds on Crete and on the mainland, ​and two ‌more were lightly injured.

events.title: Tens of thousands of French wildfire evacuees allowed to return home
events.summary: French authorities gave the go-ahead Thursday for 84,000 evacuees forced out by a monster wildfire to go back to their homes in southwest France, the strongest sign yet that firefighters are turning a corner in their battle against the flames that have burned an area four times the size of Paris. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland reports.

events.title: Poland says giant crater left by explosion after Russia attacks on Ukraine
events.summary: Polish authorities said Thursday that a 10 metre (33 feet) wide crater had been left by an explosion in an eastern region that occurred as Russia staged new missile attacks on neighbouring Ukraine. Polish authorities did not immediately give the cause of the crater but it took place as Russia stage a massive new attack on the Lviv region in western Ukraine, near the border with Poland. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Andrew Hilliar tells us more.

events.title: FIFA hit by furious backlash over plans to sell stake in competitions
events.summary: There was a furious backlash on Wednesday to FIFA's controversial plans to sell a stake in the business operations of the World Cup and its other competitions through the creation of a private subsidiary. World football's governing body had said Tuesday it would retain a majority share in FIFA Forward Enterprise but hoped to raise $4.2 billion later this year by "carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests".

events.title: Drone reveals charred forest landscape after wildfires scorch France
events.summary: Drone footage captured on Wednesday (July 29) revealed the scale of destruction left by wildfires in southwestern France, showing charred land, uprooted and burnt trees and the remains of destroyed houses near Le Temple. The blaze in the Landes area west of Bordeaux burnt through 42,000 hectares of mainly pine forest, prompting authorities to evacuate about 220,000 holidaymakers and residents. Around 60,000 have since been allowed back.

events.title: US launches wave of strikes on Iran in response to Tehran missile attack in Jordan
events.summary: The US military completed a "heavy wave of strikes" against Iran on Thursday in retaliation against Tehran targeting American bases in Jordan, as fighting intensified in the Middle East war after a nearly week-long pause. The reignited hostilities have drawn in the Islamic republic's proxies, and appear to have dashed hopes of a quick return to negotiations between the foes. US President Donald Trump had vowed to hit Iran "hard" after Tehran launched missiles at Jordan, its first regional strike in days. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.

events.title: Japan quake toll hits 34 as survivors struggle in heat

The quake caused widespread damage, flattening homes, damaging bridges, triggering fires and leaving tens of thousands of residents without power and water in temperatures forecast to hit 38C this weekend.

events.title: Cooler weather and potential rain move into the French region torched by wildfires
events.summary: Higher humidity, cooler temperatures and a forecast for rain raised hopes of relief Thursday for a parched portion of southwestern France engulfed by wildfires that have charred an area four times the size of Paris in recent weeks. Local officials reported a “rather calm" night, with a fire that has not grown beyond the 42,000 hectares already affected. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland reports from Lanton, France.

events.title: US military launches 'powerful' retaliatory strikes on Iran

events.title: Paris neighbourhoods: The charming 3rd arrondissement

From the Knights Templar to fashion designers, from royal prisoners to food lovers – not to mention fascinating and sometimes quirky museums – join us as we wander through the troisième arrondissement.

events.summary: Fires continue to rage across Europe, including in France’s wine country. NBC News’ Raf Sanchez was with firefighters and volunteers in the region as they battled the flames.

events.title: Andrea Bocelli and children’s choir perform for Pope Leo at ‘Concert for Peace’
events.summary: Tom Llamas speaks with children in the choir who were part of today’s historic ‘Concert for Peace.’ The young singers, coming from places gripped by crisis. They came together at the Pope’s summer retreat, along with Andrea Bocelli, for a very special performance.

events.title: Trump vows retaliatory strike after failed Iranian attack
events.summary: President Trump is vowing a retaliatory strike against Iran after the Iranian regime unsuccessfully attempted to attack U.S. troops. NBC News’ Garrett Haake reports.

events.title: Iran launches surprise attack on U.S. Middle East bases
events.summary: According to U.S. Central Command, Iran launched a surprise ballistic missile attack in an attempt to attack U.S. forces based in the Middle East. NBC News’ Garrett Haake explains that this marks the most significant Iranian aggression in several days.

events.title: U.S. strikes Iran after Trump reportedly issues menacing new threat
events.summary: The fighting shattered a brief period of calm after weeks of escalation between the U.S. and Iran over the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: K-pop group BTS won’t submit its music for Grammy Awards
events.summary: “I hope that music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” the group said in a statement.

events.title: At least 13 killed in Japan earthquake as rescuers search for survivors in a ‘race against time’
events.summary: Multiple people were missing a day after a magnitude-7.1 quake struck Kumamoto prefecture, partially collapsing buildings.

events.title: Major earthquake rocks southern Japan, injuring dozens
events.summary: The earthquake, which had an epicenter in the southwest part of the country, was measured at magnitude 6.8 and a depth of 10 kilometers, or just over 6 miles.

events.title: Search for North Carolina woman Liz Waddell is still a missing person case, Grenada police say
events.summary: Grenadian police said their nearly week-old search for a missing North Carolina woman is still active, with hopes of finding the swimmer alive.

events.title: Oil prices slide as U.S. and Iran pause strikes to give ‘space’ for diplomacy
events.summary: The two sides halted fire over the weekend, following 13 nights of attacks that threatened new pain for the global economy.

events.title: Berlin police kill suspect in Pride festival attack after manhunt
events.summary: Authorities say the 21-year-old was fatally shot after charging at officers with a knife, a day after an attack left one dead and 29 injured.

events.title: U.S. forgoes strikes on Iran, but conflict in the Red Sea escalates
events.summary: U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” that the pause in strikes was due to ongoing talks between the two countries.

events.title: ‘Cockroaches won’: India’s youth protest leaders declare victory as minister resigns
events.summary: India’s viral Cockroach Janta Party called off its nationwide protests Saturday after the country’s education minister resigned and the government agreed to a number of the activist movement’s demands.

events.title: U.S. launches new strikes and Trump threatens ‘massive attack’ as Iran widens war
events.summary: The United States launched a fresh barrage of strikes on Iran overnight as President Donald Trump threatened a major new escalation after Tehran opened a second front in its pressure campaign on the world economy.

events.title: No basic services and nowhere to go: How Venezuelans are living a month after the earthquakes
events.summary: We visited the ruins of a housing complex built by the Chavista regime: the now homeless residents brave the heat, humidity, and flies from their tents, as they’re promised a house by 2027.
